text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- State budget deficit cut in 1995/96 fiscal year comes from rise in oil prices, not as a result of government policy, says chairman of parliament's financial affairs committee.

- Kuwait's embassy in Amman could file a suite against Jordan's Ad-Dustour newspaper. Ad-Dustour said in January members of Kuwait's Special Forces were involved in attacks in the Central Prison against Jordanians and Palestinians serving jail sentences for helping Iraq's troops during its 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait. Kuwait has denied the report.
- Active trade at the Kuwait Stock Exchange, index up 14.8 points.
- Iran's oil minister visits Kuwait on Sunday.
- Cabinet welcomes visit by Britain's Prince Charles to Kuwait on Friday.
- Lebanese parliament speaker to visit Kuwait in March.
- Three Kuwaitis arrested for attempting to smuggle 65 cases of whisky. Kuwait bans import of alcoholic beverages in compliance with Islamic rules.
